q7.answer: The live indexer's progress is the Kafka consumer-group offset for each partition. A partition's offset is committed only up to the highest offset N such that every earlier offset in that partition has been acknowledged by the index (or by a DLQ write), so one unacknowledged offset holds the commit back. The rebuild's progress is kept separately in the rebuild state table in the ops database, which records the job id, S, the recorded offsets and the last acknowledged id.

q8.answer: Offsets for the unfinished part of the batch were never committed, so on restart the group resumes from the last committed offset and resends those events. Re-sent writes with an equal version are applied again, which is harmless, and any older versions that were already superseded come back as 409 conflicts and are counted as stale.

q9.answer: In the design, the rebuild's v4 group starts at the topic offsets recorded just before S and replays everything after them into products_v4 using the same version rules, while the backfill writes rows at version S. The catch-up stage keeps replaying until lag is under 5 s, and reconcile then checks the id sets. This is not fully closed: the snapshot and the recorded offsets may be taken at slightly different moments, so a transaction that committed near S could be missed; that is an unverified assumption that needs either a second exported-snapshot slot (DBA approval) or reliance on reconcile.

q10.answer: Every document written by the bulk copy carries version S, the WAL position recorded with the snapshot, converted to a single integer as X times 2^32 plus Y. Because of the at-least rule, any live change with a larger commit_lsn overwrites a backfill document, so the copy cannot overwrite newer data.

q11.answer: After the switch the v3 group keeps consuming, so products_v3 stays current; a rollback is one alias request that points products back to products_v3. The window ends after 48 hours, when the v3 group is stopped and products_v3 is deleted. Whether the v4 group keeps running after a rollback, and whether a second switch needs a catch-up, is an open question the plan does not decide, and drift left by the old cron is not repaired by rolling back.

q12.answer: Search is not affected, because the alias still points to products_v3 until the gate passes and the swap happens. A backfill crash resumes from the cursor in the state table with the same S, and a Kafka or index outage during catch-up or backfill backs off and retries. If the gate fails, the alias is left unchanged and catch-up continues while the failure is investigated.
